chapters.name: Signs, Signals, and Pavement Markings
chapters.summary: What sign shapes and colors mean, how to respond to steady and flashing lights and arrows, and what yellow and white lines on the road tell you.
keyPoints: An eight-sided red sign means stop. A downward-pointing triangle means yield.
The pennant-shaped NO PASSING ZONE sign is on the left side of the road. The five-sided sign means a school zone.
A flashing red light means the same as a STOP sign. A flashing yellow light means slow down and go with care.
Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes going the same way.

chapters.name: Right of Way and Intersections
chapters.summary: Who goes first at stop signs, four-way stops, roundabouts, and turns, and how to yield to pedestrians, emergency vehicles, school buses, and trains.
keyPoints: At a four-way stop, the first to arrive goes first. If two arrive together, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
For an emergency vehicle with a siren or flashing lights, pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Stop at least 10 feet from a school bus with red lights flashing and its stop arm out.

chapters.name: Speed, Passing, and Parking
chapters.summary: Pennsylvania speed limits, signaling before turns, when you may pass, and the places where you may not park.
keyPoints: When no limit is posted, the limit is 35 mph in an urban district and 55 mph in other locations (25 mph in a residential district).
Signal at least 100 feet before turning below 35 mph, and at least 300 feet at 35 mph or more.
Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant, 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, or 30 feet of a stop sign.

chapters.name: Safe Driving
chapters.summary: Following distance, headlights, driving in bad weather and work zones, sharing the road, distracted driving, and the Move Over law.
keyPoints: Keep at least a four-second following distance on dry pavement, and more on wet roads.
Turn on your headlights whenever your windshield wipers are on because of the weather.
Use low beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and within 300 feet of a vehicle you follow.

chapters.name: Learner's Permit and Junior License
chapters.summary: How the learner's permit works, the 65 hours of supervised practice, and the junior license curfew and passenger limits.
keyPoints: Drivers under 18 must hold the permit for six months and log 65 hours, including 10 at night and 5 in bad weather.
A junior license holder may not drive between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m., with a few exceptions.
For the first six months, a junior driver may carry only one passenger under 18 who is not immediate family, unless a parent or guardian is in the car.

chapters.name: Alcohol, Implied Consent, and Points
chapters.summary: Pennsylvania blood alcohol limits, the implied consent law, the point system, and the texting ban.
keyPoints: The limit is 0.08% for drivers 21 and older, 0.02% for drivers under 21, and 0.04% in a commercial vehicle.
Refusing a chemical test automatically suspends your driving privilege for one year.
Reaching 6 points for the first time means you must take a Special Point Examination or attend Driver Improvement School.
